text.p: Following are the main stories in the Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatia will start paying pensions to officials of the former Yugoslav administration but only after signing a bilateral contract on social security.
- Hoteliers from Zadar area expect 400,000 overnights this summer, twice as many as in 1996.
- The Bourse announces tougher membership rules for brokerages on Monday and analysts predict only a dozen of some 45 have a chance of surviving in the long run.
- Crisis looms within HSLS, Croatia's main opposition party, as rift deepens between two top leaders Gotovac and Budisa, says analyst and party member Ivo Banac.
- Hotel Biokovo in Makarska was sold for 5.1 million German marks and should be refurbished by June 1.
- President Franjo Tudjman is in "victorious" health, says Health Minister Andrija Hebrang.
- Croatian shipyards will not make it without state subsidies, says director of Brodosplit shipyard Srecko Kurtovic.
- Over 1,000 gather in Kumrovec, birthplace of Josip Broz Tito to commemorate 17th anniversary of his death. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
